problem.passage: Paleoclimatologists studying ice cores from a Greenland glacier have debated why a sudden cooling event roughly 8,200 years ago lasted for only about 150 years rather than persisting for millennia like earlier cold intervals. One team argues that the brief duration resulted from the rapid drainage of a single glacial lake, which released a large pulse of freshwater into the North Atlantic all at once rather than in a slow, sustained trickle. According to this view, the freshwater disrupted ocean circulation sharply but only temporarily, because once the lake had fully drained, the source of freshwater disappeared and circulation patterns were able to reestablish themselves relatively quickly. A competing team contends that the short duration instead reflects the limited total volume of freshwater involved, proposing that the lake held less water overall than researchers had previously estimated, so that even sustained drainage over decades would not have been enough to disrupt circulation for more than a couple of centuries. Researchers on the first team have recently published new sediment analyses from the lake basin.
problem.stimulus: Paleoclimatologists studying ice cores from a Greenland glacier have debated why a sudden cooling event roughly 8,200 years ago lasted for only about 150 years rather than persisting for millennia like earlier cold intervals. One team argues that the brief duration resulted from the rapid drainage of a single glacial lake, which released a large pulse of freshwater into the North Atlantic all at once rather than in a slow, sustained trickle. According to this view, the freshwater disrupted ocean circulation sharply but only temporarily, because once the lake had fully drained, the source of freshwater disappeared and circulation patterns were able to reestablish themselves relatively quickly. A competing team contends that the short duration instead reflects the limited total volume of freshwater involved, proposing that the lake held less water overall than researchers had previously estimated, so that even sustained drainage over decades would not have been enough to disrupt circulation for more than a couple of centuries. Researchers on the first team have recently published new sediment analyses from the lake basin.
problem.question: Which finding from the sediment analyses, if true, would most directly support the first team's claim that the brief duration of the cooling event resulted from a rapid, one-time drainage event rather than a limited total volume of freshwater?
options: The lake basin's sediment layers show a single, sharply defined erosional channel consistent with one abrupt drainage episode rather than gradual seepage over many years.
The lake basin's total capacity, calculated from its sediment boundaries, was smaller than earlier estimates had assumed.
The lake basin's sediment layers show a single erosional channel, but radiometric dating indicates the drainage occurred several centuries before the onset of the cooling event.
The sediment layers in the lake basin show that drainage occurred in several distinct pulses spread across roughly a decade, rather than in one instantaneous event.
problem.explanation: 첫 번째 연구팀의 주장은 '호수의 물이 서서히가 아니라 한꺼번에 급격히 방류되어 해양 순환을 짧고 강하게 교란했다가 빠르게 회복되었다'는 것이다. 정답인 A는 침전물 분석에서 지속적인 침식이 아니라 단 하나의 뚜렷한 침식 통로(급격한 단발성 배수의 증거)가 발견되었다고 말하므로, 이 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침한다. B는 오히려 두 번째 팀(총 담수량이 적었다는 주장)을 지지하는 근거이므로 첫 번째 팀 주장과 모순된다. C는 이 호수가 아니라 다른 호수에 관한 것으로, 여러 차례에 걸친 배수를 보여주어 오히려 '한 번에 몰아친 배수'라는 주장과 무관하거나 반대된다. D는 침전물의 화학적 유사성에 관한 것으로 배수 방식(단발성 대 지속적)과는 관련이 없어 질문에 답하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The first team's claim is that the lake drained all at once, sharply disrupting ocean circulation before it could quickly recover, rather than releasing water slowly over a long period. Choice A directly supports this because a single, sharply defined erosional channel is physical evidence of one abrupt drainage episode rather than gradual seepage. Choice B actually supports the competing team's claim about limited total volume, so it contradicts the first team's position. Choice C describes a different lake with multiple smaller drainage events over time, which is irrelevant to (or even undercuts) the claim of a single abrupt drainage of this lake. Choice D concerns chemical similarity between sediment layers from different cooling events, which does not address the mechanism of drainage (sudden versus gradual) at all, so it fails to answer the question.
problem.evidenceTarget: the first team's claim that the brief duration of the cooling event resulted from a rapid, one-time drainage event rather than a limited total volume of freshwater
problem.evidenceSpan: the brief duration resulted from the rapid drainage of a single glacial lake, which released a large pulse of freshwater into the North Atlantic all at once rather than in a slow, sustained trickle
problem.answerRationale: 정답 선택지는 침전물에 '단 한 번의 급격한 배수'를 뒷받침하는 뚜렷한 단일 침식 통로가 있다고 명시하여, 첫 번째 연구팀이 주장하는 '한 번에 몰아친 대량 방류' 가설을 직접적으로 확증한다.

difficultyReasons: 첫 번째 팀과 경쟁 팀의 주장을 정확히 구분해야 함(화자 관점 구분)
선택지 C처럼 표면적으로는 첫 번째 팀 주장과 일치하나 시간적 인과관계를 뒤집는 세부 정보를 포착해야 하므로 추론 2단계 이상 필요
선택지 B는 명백히 경쟁팀 주장이라 쉽게 제거 가능하나, C는 꼼꼼히 읽어야 오답임을 알 수 있어 전체 난이도를 medium으로 유지

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에 나온 '경쟁팀'의 주장인 호수 용량이 작았다는 내용을 그대로 반영하고 있어 관련 있어 보인다
distractors.matches: 두 번째 팀(경쟁팀)의 주장과 일치하는 정보
distractors.whyWrong: 이는 첫 번째 팀이 아니라 경쟁 팀의 주장을 뒷받침하는 근거이므로 질문에서 요구하는 첫 번째 팀 지지 근거가 아니다

distractors.plausibleBecause: 단일 침식 채널이라는 첫 부분은 첫 번째 팀 주장과 일치해 보여 그럴듯하다
distractors.matches: 단일 배수 사건이라는 부분은 첫 번째 팀 주장과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 방사성 연대측정 결과 배수가 냉각 사건 발생보다 수백 년 앞서 일어났다는 것은 배수와 냉각 사이의 인과관계 자체를 부정하는 것이므로, 오히려 첫 번째 팀의 주장을 약화시킨다

distractors.plausibleBecause: 호수 배수와 관련된 침전물 분석 결과라는 점에서 관련 있어 보이고, 수십 년에 걸친 지속적 배수라는 표현이 지문의 표현과 유사해 혼동될 수 있다
distractors.matches: 침전물 층에서 배수 패턴을 분석했다는 점에서 소재가 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 여러 차례에 걸친 배수는 첫 번째 팀이 주장하는 '단번의 급격한 배수'가 아니라 오히려 지속적이고 점진적인 배수를 시사하므로 첫 번째 팀의 주장과 정반대된다
